If Bernie wants to fix the country here's what he needs to do:

  • It needs to be put into law that all corporations follow International Financial Reporting Standards, so as to create transparency.

  • There should be stricter regulations on the banking system in general. Canada for example did not have a failing in its banking system, and they did not need bail outs. America could copy them.

  • Universal health care ought be put into place.

  • There should be reasonable caps on real estate prices, determined for each particular market. Obviously, you have to take into account demand, and difference in value.

  • We need expansion of high speed public transportation. That should be a priority, especially for densely populated locations.

  • Subsidies on healthy foods, so that they will be competitive to junk food calorie-wise. To balance this out, place extra taxes on sugary, and high fat foods.

  • Outlaw data caps, because internet, and computer based information exchange is the achilles heel of technology. Again, an addendum, there still needs to be guarantees on speed. An ISP shouldn't be able to for example slow you down to 56 KBPS or something ridiculous as that. There has to be a reasonable minimum.

  • There should be free online university for everyone. From a taxpayer's perspective this is much more manageable than having physical schools to serve the educational needs of individuals. You can definitely make it online, and stay within a tight budget. Online schools have already been prove to work and are far more cost-effective. If were are to be concerned about cheating, then pre-existing infrastructures can be used to hold examinations.

  • Labor laws need to be tightened up. Workers for example should be able to get up to 15 sick days off, and receive half their regular wages during those recovery periods. Also, all companies should have to have a revenue sharing plan, which would be equally split amongst workers. This is actually a very clever way to avoid the minimum wage conundrum. If times are bad employers pay out less. If times are good, then workers prosper along with the company automatically. Let's take Wal-Mart for example. Let's say you took 5% of all revenue, and split it evenly amongst workers. This would be equal to $11,000 extra, annually, for each worker. That's not an insignificant sum.
